items.comment: Accurate: `"" + obj` invokes String.valueOf(obj), so the message is indeed the string representation of `obj`, and a null `obj` does yield the literal message "null". First sentence stands alone, backticks used correctly, @param tag has no trailing period as expected for a phrase continuation.

items.declaration: object UninitializedFieldError: override def toString(): String = "UninitializedFieldError"
items.comment: Verified against scala.Function1 (toString overridden there to "<function1>") and scala.runtime.AbstractFunction1 (does not itself override toString, so it inherits Function1's). The claim that toString is 'inherited via AbstractFunction1 from Function1' and would otherwise render as `<function1>` is accurate. Wiki-style links used correctly for both referenced types; description begins with "Returns" and fully states the return, so omitting an explicit @return is correct per convention.

bonus_findings.issue: Opens with 'This class implements errors which are thrown whenever...' — a needless self-referential construction ('This class ...') that the style guide discourages in favor of a direct declarative statement (e.g. 'Signals that a field was used before it was initialized.'). Not part of the reviewed diff, so not scored, but worth a human note for a future pass.
